ExoPlain: An Interactive, Explainable AI Platform
for Exoplanet Discovery
From TESS light curves and candidate parameters to interpretable evidence for human review

Planet Pioneers · Student research team · NASA Space Apps Challenge 2025
Authors: [student names] · School: [school] · Mentor: [mentor]

Transit surveys produce large time-series datasets, but a brightness dip alone does not confirm a planet. Stellar variability, eclipsing binaries, instrumental noise and processing artifacts can create similar signatures. ExoPlain connects candidate measurements, FITS processing, experimental classifiers and a language-model explanation layer so learners can trace how an input becomes an assessment.
Research question: How can an interactive AI system make exoplanet evidence easier to interpret while preserving uncertainty and the distinction between screening and confirmation?
Upload FITS or enter 16 orbital, transit, stellar and position fields.
Select TIME/flux columns, remove invalid rows and median-normalize.
Interpolate to 2,048 points and compute 37 engineered features.
Scale features, run Random Forest and compare sequence models.
Send labeled evidence to Gemini for a readable assessment.

Current architecture has two paths. Manual candidate entry calls Gemini directly. FITS upload calls the Python feature service and Random Forest. The production goal is one auditable pipeline in which the classifier supplies evidence and the language model explains it.

Training scripts use TESS light curves and TFOPWG dispositions. CP/KP/PC map to positive; FP/Unknown map to negative. Documentation reports 7,638 curves and strong class imbalance. Provenance and target grouping require audit.
The FITS service finds common time and flux columns, removes NaN/Inf samples, requires at least 100 valid points, normalizes by median flux and linearly interpolates every curve to 2,048 points.
The feature path standardizes 37 engineered variables and trains class-balanced trees with a stratified 80/20 split. The model stores feature importance and AUC metadata.
The 1D CNN uses five convolution blocks: 64, 128, 256, 512 and 512 channels. LSTM downsamples to 256 timesteps with 32 hidden units. An MLP provides a dense baseline.
Seed 42, Adam with learning rate 10⁻³, weight decay 10⁻⁴, ReduceLROnPlateau, early stopping, gradient clipping, dropout and augmentation.
Inputs include period, epoch, impact parameter, duration, depth, radius, temperature, insolation, SNR, stellar properties, magnitude and sky position. Transit depth δ ≈ (Rₚ/R★)².

Distribution statistics · dip/peak counts at 1σ-3σ · three depth proxies · variance/RMSE · skewness/kurtosis · dominant frequency and band powers · rolling statistics · trend/R² · autocorrelation at lags 1/5/10 · periodicity strength
Manual form, FITS upload, 3D exploration and results interface.
Format measurements and call Gemini 2.5 Pro.
Parse FITS, normalize, resample, extract features and run RF.
Serialized RF/scaler plus CNN, LSTM and MLP checkpoints.
Manual entry sends submitted measurements. FITS analysis sends labeled features and Random Forest probability.
Gemini returns a Boolean assessment and five important features with relevance descriptions.
Users connect the assessment to transit depth, periodicity, stellar context and signal quality.
The explanation supports learning and candidate triage, not scientific confirmation.

The manual Gemini route maps answers to fixed 85%/15% confidence and defaults missing answers toward true. The upload route can return randomized fallback features when the Python service fails. Both behaviors must be removed or visibly labeled before scientific use.
Manual input, FITS upload, results and 3D exploration
RF, CNN, LSTM and MLP code with checkpoints
README reports 7,638 TESS curves and 95.4% positives
CNN loss and RF AUC reported in repository
No grouped held-out test or calibration analysis
Record TIC IDs, sectors, label source and dates. Resolve Unknown labels and duplicates.
Group observations by star so repeat sectors cannot enter both train and test.
Compare every model with simple rules and remove feature families one at a time.
Report reliability curves, Brier score and threshold tradeoffs.
Test on a later sector or independently curated candidate set.
Measure whether students identify evidence, uncertainty and follow-up needs.
ROC-AUC and PR-AUC · precision, recall and F1 · confusion matrix · calibration and Brier score · latency · failure examples
Present outputs as candidate-screening evidence, publish calibrated uncertainty, disclose fallbacks and require human review before confirmation.

ExoPlain connects raw exoplanet evidence, machine-learning predictions and readable explanations in one learning workflow. The next priority is rigorous validation, calibrated uncertainty and removal of simulated fallbacks.

Scientific context: NASA Exoplanet Archive, TESS and TFOPWG dispositions. Repository-reported model values have not been independently reproduced.
